monday.definition: The day after Sunday and before Tuesday.

tuesday.definition: The day after Monday and before Wednesday.

wednesday.definition: The day after Tuesday and before Thursday.

thursday.definition: The day after Wednesday and before Friday.

friday.definition: The day after Thursday and before Saturday.

saturday.definition: The day after Friday and before Sunday.

sunday.definition: The day after Saturday and before Monday.

weekday.definition: A day that is not part of the weekend in a particular place.
weekday.arabicTranslation: يوم من أيام الأسبوع غير عطلة نهاية الأسبوع

weekend.definition: The days at the end of a working week when many people do not work.

day-off.definition: A day when a person does not have to go to work or school.

leap-year.definition: A year with 366 days, including an extra day in February.

fiscal-year.definition: A twelve-month period used to plan and report an organization's finances.

academic-year.definition: The part of the year when a school or university holds classes.

calendar-year.definition: The twelve-month period from January 1 to December 31.

quarter.definition: One of four three-month periods in a year.

today.definition: The day that is happening now.

tomorrow.definition: The day immediately after the present day.

date.definition: A particular day shown by its day, month, and year.

appointment.definition: A planned meeting with a person at a particular time.

planner.definition: A notebook or calendar used to organize tasks, dates, and appointments.

diary.definition: A book in which someone writes about what happens each day.

agenda.definition: A list of topics to discuss during a meeting.

schedule.definition: A plan that shows when activities or events will happen.

event.definition: Something planned to happen at a particular time, such as a celebration or meeting.

banana.definition: A long, curved fruit with yellow skin and soft, sweet flesh.

orange.definition: A round citrus fruit with orange skin and juicy sections inside.

grape.definition: A small, round fruit that grows in bunches and can be green or purple.

watermelon.definition: A large fruit with green skin, red or yellow flesh, and many seeds.

pineapple.definition: A large tropical fruit with rough skin, yellow flesh, and pointed leaves.

mango.definition: A sweet tropical fruit with yellow-orange flesh and one large seed.

peach.definition: A soft, sweet fruit with fuzzy skin and one large stone inside.

pear.definition: A sweet fruit with a narrow top and rounded bottom.

blackberry.definition: A soft, dark-purple berry made of many small juicy parts.

cranberry.definition: A small, tart red berry often used in juice or sauce.

gooseberry.definition: A small green or red berry with a tart taste, often used in jam.

mulberry.definition: A small, sweet berry that grows on a tree and can be red, purple, or black.

boysenberry.definition: A large, dark berry related to blackberries and raspberries.

lingonberry.definition: A small, tart red berry that grows on low plants in northern regions.

elderberry.definition: A small, dark berry from the elder tree, often cooked into syrup or jam.

papaya.definition: A tropical fruit with yellow-orange skin, orange flesh, and black seeds.

passion-fruit.definition: A round tropical fruit with a tough skin and fragrant, seedy pulp inside.

guava.definition: A round tropical fruit with green or yellow skin and fragrant flesh.

coconut.definition: A large brown fruit with a hard shell, white flesh, and liquid inside.

lychee.definition: A small fruit with rough red skin, sweet white flesh, and one seed.

star-fruit.definition: A yellow tropical fruit whose slices look like stars.

jackfruit.definition: A very large tropical fruit with a rough skin and sweet yellow pieces inside.

durian.definition: A large tropical fruit with a spiky shell and strong-smelling flesh.

rambutan.definition: A small tropical fruit with a red hairy skin and sweet white flesh.

lemon.definition: A yellow citrus fruit with sour juice.

lime.definition: A small green citrus fruit with sour juice.

grapefruit.definition: A large citrus fruit with a thick rind and tart pink or yellow flesh.

tangerine.definition: A small orange citrus fruit with sweet flesh and easy-to-peel skin.

mandarin.definition: A small sweet citrus fruit with a loose, easy-to-peel orange skin.

kumquat.definition: A small orange citrus fruit that can be eaten with its sweet peel.

pomelo.definition: A very large citrus fruit with thick skin and pale, mildly sweet sections.

clementine.definition: A small, sweet type of mandarin orange with thin, easy-to-peel skin.

blood-orange.definition: A type of orange with red or dark-red flesh inside.

cherry.definition: A small, round fruit with red or dark skin and one hard stone inside.

plum.definition: A small, smooth-skinned fruit with sweet flesh and one stone inside.

apricot.definition: A small orange fruit with soft skin, sweet flesh, and one stone inside.

nectarine.definition: A sweet fruit like a peach but with smooth skin.

date.definition: A small, sweet brown fruit that grows on a palm tree.

fig.definition: A soft fruit with thin skin and many tiny seeds inside.

avocado.definition: A fruit with green flesh, thick skin, and one large seed.

persimmon.definition: A sweet orange fruit with smooth skin and soft flesh when ripe.

olive.definition: A small green or black fruit often eaten after curing or pressed for oil.

pomegranate.definition: A round fruit with a thick skin and many juicy red seeds inside.

beet.definition: A round root vegetable with dark-red flesh, often eaten cooked or raw.

turnip.definition: A round root vegetable with white or purple skin and pale flesh.

radish.definition: A small, crisp root vegetable with a sharp taste, often eaten raw.

parsnip.definition: A pale root vegetable shaped like a carrot, with a sweet taste.

yam.definition: A starchy edible tuber with rough skin, often cooked like a potato.

rutabaga.definition: A large round root vegetable with purple skin and yellow flesh.

ginger.definition: A knobby, spicy root used to flavor food and drinks.
ginger.exampleUsage: She grated fresh ginger into the soup.

spinach.definition: A leafy green vegetable eaten raw or cooked.

kale.definition: A leafy green vegetable with curly leaves.

arugula.definition: A leafy salad vegetable with a slightly peppery taste.

cabbage.definition: A leafy vegetable with a tightly packed, round head.

chard.definition: A leafy green vegetable with broad leaves and thick edible stems.

romaine.definition: A type of lettuce with long, crisp leaves.

watercress.definition: A leafy green vegetable that grows in water and has a peppery taste.

broccoli.definition: A green vegetable with a thick stem and clusters of small flower buds.

cauliflower.definition: A vegetable with a firm white head made of tightly packed flower buds.

kohlrabi.definition: A vegetable with a round, swollen stem and crisp flesh.

zucchini.definition: A long green summer squash with soft skin, eaten cooked or raw.

cucumber.definition: A long green vegetable with crisp, watery flesh, often eaten raw.

gourd.definition: A fruit with a hard shell, grown for food, containers, or decoration.

bell-pepper.definition: A mild, hollow pepper that may be green, red, yellow, or orange.

chili-pepper.definition: A small pepper with a hot taste, used to add heat to food.

eggplant.definition: A vegetable with smooth, usually purple skin and soft flesh when cooked.

serrano.definition: A small, hot chili pepper that is green or red.

paprika.definition: A red spice made from dried and ground peppers.

garlic.definition: A strongly flavored bulb made of cloves, used to season food.

leek.definition: A vegetable with a long white stem and flat green leaves, related to onions.

shallot.definition: A small onion-like vegetable with a mild flavor, used in cooking.

scallion.definition: A young onion with a long green stem and a small white base.

chive.definition: A thin green herb with a mild onion flavor, often cut into small pieces.

asparagus.definition: A green vegetable eaten as young, tender stalks.

celery.definition: A crisp vegetable with long pale-green stalks and leaves.

artichoke.definition: A vegetable with thick leaves surrounding a tender edible center.

fennel.definition: A vegetable with a pale bulb and feathery leaves, with a mild anise flavor.

million.exampleUsage: More than one million people live in the city.

percentage.exampleUsage: A high percentage of the class passed the test.

novel.exampleUsage: She borrowed a novel about a family adventure.

encyclopedia.exampleUsage: He used an encyclopedia to learn about planets.

atlas.exampleUsage: She opened the atlas to find a map of Africa.

biography.exampleUsage: He read a biography of a famous scientist.

step-stool.definition: A small stool with one or two steps, used to reach high shelves.
step-stool.exampleUsage: The librarian used a step stool to reach the top shelf.

cart.definition: A wheeled frame used to move books and other items around a library.
cart.exampleUsage: The librarian pushed a cart of books between the shelves.

armchair.exampleUsage: She sat in an armchair to read by the window.

fiction.exampleUsage: The fiction shelves contain made-up stories.

non-fiction.exampleUsage: He chose a non-fiction book about birds.

periodicals.definition: Magazines and newspapers published regularly, such as every week or month.
periodicals.exampleUsage: The newest periodicals are displayed near the entrance.

media-center.definition: A room with books, computers, and other media for learning and research.
media-center.exampleUsage: The students used computers in the media center.

help-desk.definition: A counter where library staff answer questions and help visitors find resources.
help-desk.exampleUsage: Ask at the help desk if you cannot find a book.

archive.exampleUsage: The archive holds old photographs and letters.

reading.exampleUsage: Reading helps her learn new words.

borrowing.definition: Taking a library item home for a limited time and returning it later.
borrowing.exampleUsage: Borrowing books is free with a library card.

returning.definition: Bringing a borrowed library item back after using it.
returning.exampleUsage: Returning books on time helps other readers.

searching.exampleUsage: She is searching the catalog for a history book.

studying.exampleUsage: The students are studying quietly at the tables.

browsing.definition: Looking through books or shelves without searching for one specific title.
browsing.exampleUsage: He spent an hour browsing the new books.

reserving.definition: Asking the library to hold a book so you can borrow it later.
reserving.exampleUsage: Reserving the book means she can collect it when it is available.

typing.exampleUsage: He is typing a search term into the catalog.

whispering.definition: Speaking very quietly so that other people in the library are not disturbed.
whispering.exampleUsage: The children were whispering in the reading room.

bookmark.exampleUsage: She placed a bookmark between the pages.

book-cover.definition: The protective outer part of a book that shows its title and often a picture.
book-cover.exampleUsage: The book cover shows a bright picture of the sea.

librarian.exampleUsage: The librarian helped him find a book.

assistant.exampleUsage: The assistant returned the books to their shelves.

reader.exampleUsage: The reader sat quietly with a book.

researcher.definition: A person who studies a subject carefully to discover or check information.
researcher.exampleUsage: The researcher examined old newspapers in the library.

author.definition: A person who writes a book, story, or other written work.
author.exampleUsage: The author signed her new book at the library.

storyteller.exampleUsage: The storyteller read a tale to the children.

cleaner.definition: A person who cleans the library and keeps its rooms tidy.
cleaner.exampleUsage: The cleaner wiped the tables after closing time.

reference-book.definition: A book used to look up facts, such as a dictionary or encyclopedia.
reference-book.exampleUsage: She checked a reference book to confirm the date.

stamp.definition: A small tool used to print an official mark on a library item or paper.
stamp.exampleUsage: The librarian used a stamp to mark the return date.

catalog.definition: A searchable list of the books and other items held by a library.
catalog.exampleUsage: He searched the catalog for books about space.

computer.definition: An electronic device used to search the catalog, read, or write.
computer.exampleUsage: She used the computer to search for a book.

printer.definition: A machine that produces paper copies of documents or pictures.
printer.exampleUsage: He printed his assignment using the library printer.

guard.definition: A person who watches over the library and helps keep people and property safe.
guard.exampleUsage: The guard checked the entrance before closing.
